steps: The primary accepts v2 while replicas still expose v1.
Replica A receives and applies v2 after propagation delay.
Replica B remains stale briefly, then receives the update.
With no new writes, every replica converges to v2 at Tn.

lesson.scenario: A profile display name propagates asynchronously from a home replica to two remote replicas.

steps.title: Common baseline
steps.narration: Every replica stores display name Ana at version 42.
steps.invariant: Convergence is defined relative to a quiescent update stream and successful delivery.

steps.title: Local write
steps.narration: The home replica commits display name Anika as version 43.
steps.outcome: Remote reads may now return stale version 42.

steps.title: First propagation
steps.outcome: EU converges while APAC remains stale.
steps.invariant: A newer version must not be overwritten by an older delivery.

steps.title: Delayed replica catches up
steps.narration: APAC receives the queued mutation after a transient delay.
steps.outcome: All replicas expose the same value.
steps.invariant: If updates stop and messages arrive, replicas must converge.

steps.title: Anti-entropy verifies
steps.narration: A digest exchange confirms no replica is missing version 43.
steps.outcome: Convergence is detected rather than assumed.
steps.invariant: Eventual consistency alone provides no maximum staleness duration.
